plan.title: Explore workspace structure and existing artifacts
plan.description: List all files/directories in data/, examine existing yaml configs, existing train/val splits, and any pre-trained models or labels. Check what has already been set up (data_sc.yaml, data_multiclass.yaml, labels directories, etc.). Read annotations.json to understand category distribution, image sizes, annotation density.
plan.success_criteria: Complete inventory of workspace: existing splits, configs, label formats, pre-computed assets. Understanding of annotation stats (categories, images, boxes per image, class frequency distribution).

plan.title: Verify package versions and GPU availability
plan.description: Check installed versions of ultralytics, torch, torchvision, timm, pycocotools, ensemble-boxes. Install ultralytics==8.1.0 if needed. Verify GPU access (torch.cuda.is_available(), GPU name, VRAM). Check if any pre-trained YOLO weights exist in workspace.
plan.success_criteria: All critical packages at correct versions. GPU confirmed available with specs logged.

plan.title: Examine existing data splits and YOLO label directories
plan.description: Read val_split.json and train_split.json to understand the existing 90/10 split. Check how many images in each, category coverage. Examine labels_yolov8x_1280/ and labels_sc/ directories to see if YOLO-format labels already exist. Check data yaml files for paths and class counts.
plan.success_criteria: Understand existing split (seed, stratification, image counts). Know if YOLO labels are pre-generated for both multiclass and single-class settings.

plan.title: Examine reference product images and metadata
plan.description: Explore data/products/ directory structure. Count how many products have reference images, how many images per product, image quality/size. Read metadata.json to understand product names, annotation counts, available image types. Identify which categories have good reference coverage vs sparse.
plan.success_criteria: Know reference image availability per category. Understand metadata structure. Identify categories with 0 reference images.

plan.title: Build evaluation function
plan.description: Write a robust evaluation function using pycocotools that computes: (1) detection_mAP@0.5 (all predictions mapped to single category), (2) classification_mAP@0.5 (original category_ids), (3) val_score = 0.7*det + 0.3*cls. Test it with dummy predictions to verify correctness. Save as reusable utility.
plan.success_criteria: Evaluation function works correctly on dummy data, handles edge cases (empty predictions, missing categories), and produces reproducible scores.

plan.title: Baseline: YOLOv8n multiclass (nc=357) at 640px
plan.hypothesis: A small YOLOv8n baseline at 640px establishes a lower bound, likely val_score ~0.15-0.30 given the difficulty.
plan.description: Train YOLOv8n with nc=357 on the training split at imgsz=640 for 100 epochs. Use existing data yaml and labels. Evaluate on val split using the evaluation function. Record val_score, detection_mAP, classification_mAP, training time, and model size.
plan.success_criteria: Baseline val_score recorded. Training completes without errors.

plan.title: Baseline: YOLOv8x multiclass (nc=357) at 1280px
plan.hypothesis: YOLOv8x at 1280px should significantly outperform YOLOv8n due to more capacity and higher resolution for dense small products.
plan.description: Train YOLOv8x with nc=357 at imgsz=1280 for 300 epochs. Use close_mosaic=50, appropriate batch size for A800 80GB. Evaluate on val split. Compare to baseline.
plan.success_criteria: val_score significantly higher than YOLOv8n baseline. Record all metrics.

plan.title: Single-class detector: YOLOv8x nc=1 at 1280px
plan.hypothesis: A single-class detector should achieve higher detection recall since it doesn't need to distinguish 357 categories, giving a higher detection_mAP@0.5.
plan.description: Train YOLOv8x with nc=1 (all annotations as one class) at imgsz=1280 for 300 epochs. Evaluate detection_mAP@0.5 only. Compare detection performance to the multiclass model.
plan.success_criteria: Detection mAP@0.5 is higher than the multiclass model's detection mAP. Record the gap.

plan.title: DINOv2-base embedding gallery construction
plan.hypothesis: DINOv2 embeddings from reference product images and training crops can enable nearest-neighbor classification that outperforms YOLO's built-in classification for rare categories.
plan.description: Build a DINOv2-base embedding gallery: (1) Extract crops from training images using GT annotations, (2) Extract embeddings from reference product images in data/products/, (3) Store gallery as {category_id: [embeddings]}. Test kNN classification (k=5) on val split crops (using GT boxes first to isolate classification quality).
plan.success_criteria: Gallery built successfully. Classification accuracy on GT-box val crops measured and compared to YOLO multiclass predictions on same crops.

plan.title: Two-stage pipeline: nc=1 YOLO + DINOv2 classification
plan.hypothesis: Combining the best detector (nc=1) with DINOv2 classification should yield a higher val_score than either the multiclass YOLO alone or detection-only (capped at 0.70).
plan.description: Use the nc=1 detector from step 8 to get detection boxes on val images. For each detected box, crop from the original full-resolution image, compute DINOv2-base embedding, classify via kNN against the gallery. Compute full val_score. Compare to multiclass YOLO.
plan.success_criteria: val_score exceeds the multiclass YOLO baseline. Classification adds meaningful score above the 0.70 detection-only cap.

plan.title: Confidence-gated classification: YOLO classes vs DINOv2
plan.hypothesis: Using YOLO's class predictions when confident and DINOv2 when YOLO is uncertain should outperform either alone.
plan.description: For each detection from the multiclass YOLO model: if YOLO class confidence > threshold T, use YOLO's category_id; else use DINOv2 kNN classification. Sweep T from 0.1 to 0.9 on val split. Also try: always use DINOv2, always use YOLO, and the gated approach.
plan.success_criteria: Find optimal threshold T. Gated approach achieves higher classification_mAP than either method alone.

plan.title: NMS and score threshold tuning
plan.hypothesis: Default NMS IoU=0.7 and conf=0.25 may not be optimal for dense shelves. Lower conf threshold increases recall; adjusted NMS handles touching products better.
plan.description: Using the best detector so far, sweep: conf_threshold in [0.05, 0.1, 0.15, 0.2, 0.25, 0.3], NMS IoU threshold in [0.4, 0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8]. Evaluate val_score for each combination. Also try max_det values [300, 500, 1000] since images have ~91 annotations on average.
plan.success_criteria: Find optimal conf/NMS/max_det settings. Improvement over defaults quantified.

plan.title: Test-time augmentation (TTA)
plan.hypothesis: TTA (multi-scale + flip) should improve detection mAP by 1-2 points at the cost of ~3x inference time.
plan.description: Run the best detector with augment=True on val split. Measure detection_mAP improvement and wall-clock time increase. Estimate if TTA fits within the 300s inference budget for ~25 test images (extrapolate to full test set).
plan.success_criteria: TTA improves detection_mAP. Inference time is feasible within 300s budget.

plan.title: SAHI-style tiled inference
plan.hypothesis: Slicing images into overlapping 1280×1280 tiles and running detection on each tile should dramatically improve detection of small products that are lost at full-image resize.
plan.description: Implement tiled inference: slice each ~2000×1500 image into overlapping tiles (1280×1280, stride 960), run detector on each tile + full image, merge predictions using WBF from ensemble-boxes. Evaluate on val split. Measure detection_mAP improvement and inference time.
plan.success_criteria: Detection mAP improves over single-pass inference. Inference time is feasible.

plan.title: YOLOv8l vs YOLOv8x comparison
plan.hypothesis: YOLOv8l may achieve similar detection quality to YOLOv8x while being faster and smaller, leaving more budget for ensemble or larger DINOv2.
plan.description: Train YOLOv8l with same settings as YOLOv8x (nc=1 or nc=357, whichever was better). Compare val_score, inference speed, and model size. Calculate if the savings enable a better overall pipeline.
plan.success_criteria: Quantified tradeoff: val_score difference, speed difference, size difference between l and x.

plan.title: RT-DETR-l training and evaluation
plan.hypothesis: RT-DETR (transformer-based) has different error patterns than YOLO and may perform better on dense overlapping objects, making it a good ensemble partner.
plan.description: Train RT-DETR-l (available in ultralytics 8.1.0) with nc=1 at imgsz=1280 for 300 epochs. Evaluate standalone detection_mAP and val_score (with DINOv2 classification). Compare to YOLO.
plan.success_criteria: RT-DETR-l trained successfully. Standalone performance and error patterns compared to YOLO.

plan.title: WBF ensemble: YOLO + RT-DETR
plan.hypothesis: Ensembling architecturally diverse models (YOLO + RT-DETR) with WBF should improve detection mAP by 2-4 points over the best single model.
plan.description: Run both YOLOv8x and RT-DETR-l on val images. Merge predictions using WBF from ensemble-boxes. Sweep WBF IoU threshold and model weights. Evaluate val_score with DINOv2 classification on merged boxes.
plan.success_criteria: Ensemble val_score exceeds best single model. Optimal WBF parameters identified.

plan.title: DINOv2 kNN hyperparameter tuning
plan.hypothesis: Tuning k, distance metric, and temperature for softmax-weighted voting can improve classification mAP by 1-3 points.
plan.description: Sweep kNN parameters on val split using GT boxes: k in [1, 3, 5, 7, 11, 15], distance metrics [cosine, L2], temperature for softmax weighting [0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.5], and distance-weighted vs majority voting. Also test gallery composition: reference-only, crops-only, mixed with different weightings.
plan.success_criteria: Optimal kNN configuration found. Classification accuracy improvement quantified.

plan.title: DINOv2-large vs DINOv2-base comparison
plan.hypothesis: DINOv2-large produces better embeddings for fine-grained product distinction, improving classification_mAP by 3-5 points.
plan.description: Build gallery with DINOv2-large (ViT-L/14). Compare classification accuracy on val GT crops vs DINOv2-base. Measure model size and inference time. Determine if it fits within 420MB budget alongside the detector.
plan.success_criteria: Classification improvement quantified. Size/speed feasibility assessed.

plan.title: Fine-tuned projection head on DINOv2 embeddings
plan.hypothesis: A small MLP trained with ArcFace/SupCon loss on DINOv2 features can learn to separate visually similar products better than raw embeddings.
plan.description: Freeze DINOv2-base, train a 2-layer MLP projection head (768→512→256) using ArcFace loss on training crops + reference images. Use the projected embeddings for kNN classification. Compare to raw DINOv2 embeddings on val split.
plan.success_criteria: Projected embeddings achieve higher classification accuracy than raw embeddings.

plan.title: Gallery composition optimization
plan.hypothesis: The ratio and weighting of reference images vs training crops in the gallery significantly affects classification quality.
plan.description: Test gallery variants: (1) reference images only, (2) training crops only, (3) mixed with reference weight 1.0 and crop weight 1.0, (4) reference repeated 3x, (5) reference + augmented reference (flips, brightness). Evaluate each on val split classification accuracy.
plan.success_criteria: Best gallery composition identified with measurable improvement.

plan.title: Multi-crop embedding inference
plan.hypothesis: Averaging embeddings from multiple slight crop variations reduces sensitivity to exact box boundaries and improves classification.
plan.description: For each detection, extract 3-5 crop variations: original, center-zoomed (80% of box), padded (120% of box), left-shifted, right-shifted. Average their DINOv2 embeddings before gallery lookup. Compare to single-crop on val split.
plan.success_criteria: Multi-crop improves classification accuracy over single-crop.

plan.title: Training at higher resolution (1600 or 1920)
plan.hypothesis: Training at 1600+ resolution preserves more product detail and improves detection of small/dense products.
plan.description: Train YOLOv8x (or best model size) at imgsz=1600 with reduced batch size and gradient accumulation. Compare detection_mAP to 1280 training. If 1600 works, try 1920.
plan.success_criteria: Higher resolution training improves detection_mAP. Training is feasible on A800 80GB.

plan.title: Training hyperparameter optimization: epochs and close_mosaic
plan.hypothesis: Longer training (500-800 epochs) with extended close_mosaic period improves final model quality for this complex dataset.
plan.description: Train with 500 epochs (close_mosaic=100) and 800 epochs (close_mosaic=150). Compare to 300-epoch baseline. Monitor for overfitting via val loss curves.
plan.success_criteria: Optimal epoch count and close_mosaic timing identified. val_score improvement quantified.

plan.title: Label smoothing and focal loss for multiclass training
plan.hypothesis: Label smoothing helps with noisy labels and visually similar categories; focal loss helps with class imbalance.
plan.description: Train YOLOv8x nc=357 with label_smoothing=0.1 and compare to no smoothing. Also test different cls_loss weights. Evaluate classification_mAP improvement.
plan.success_criteria: Label smoothing or focal loss improves classification_mAP.

plan.title: Copy-paste augmentation from reference images
plan.hypothesis: Pasting reference product images onto shelf backgrounds as synthetic training data improves detection and classification of rare categories.
plan.description: Implement copy-paste augmentation: for rare categories (appearing <5 times), paste reference product images onto random shelf image backgrounds with perspective warps and lighting adjustments. Retrain detector with augmented data. Evaluate improvement on rare categories.
plan.success_criteria: Rare category detection/classification improves. Overall val_score doesn't degrade.

plan.title: Co-occurrence priors for classification
plan.hypothesis: Products on the same shelf section tend to be from the same category group. Using co-occurrence statistics as a Bayesian prior improves classification.
plan.description: Build category co-occurrence matrix from training data (which categories appear in the same image). For each val image, after initial classification, apply co-occurrence prior: boost probability of categories that co-occur with already-confident detections. Measure classification_mAP change.
plan.success_criteria: Co-occurrence prior improves classification_mAP without hurting detection.

plan.title: Pseudo-labeling at test time
plan.hypothesis: High-confidence detections from the first pass can augment the DINOv2 gallery, improving classification of the same products in other test images.
plan.description: Implement two-pass inference: (1) Run detector + DINOv2 on all val images, (2) Add crops with score > 0.85 to the gallery, (3) Re-classify all detections with the augmented gallery. Measure val_score improvement.
plan.success_criteria: Second pass improves classification_mAP. The approach is feasible within 300s budget.

plan.title: Patch-level DINOv2 matching
plan.hypothesis: Matching individual DINOv2 patch tokens (instead of CLS token only) is more robust to partial occlusion and improves classification of occluded products.
plan.description: Extract patch-level tokens from DINOv2 for both query crops and gallery entries. Implement patch-level matching (e.g., average of top-k most similar patches). Compare to CLS-only matching on val split.
plan.success_criteria: Patch-level matching improves classification accuracy, especially for partially occluded products.

plan.title: Per-category adaptive classification thresholds
plan.hypothesis: Some products are easy to classify (unique packaging) and some are near-impossible. Adaptive thresholds per category improve overall classification_mAP.
plan.description: For each category, compute the distribution of DINOv2 similarity scores on val split. Set per-category thresholds: only assign a category if similarity exceeds its threshold. Fall back to category_id=0 for uncertain ones. Optimize thresholds to maximize classification_mAP.
plan.success_criteria: Adaptive thresholds improve classification_mAP over a single global threshold.

plan.title: Rectangular inference (rect=True)
plan.hypothesis: Rectangular inference preserves aspect ratio better than square resize, potentially improving detection on non-square images.
plan.description: Run inference with rect=True on val split. Compare detection_mAP to square inference. Measure any speed difference.
plan.success_criteria: Quantified impact of rectangular inference on detection quality.

plan.title: Image preprocessing: CLAHE contrast enhancement
plan.hypothesis: CLAHE contrast enhancement improves detection on poorly lit shelf images.
plan.description: Apply CLAHE preprocessing to val images before detection. Compare detection_mAP with and without CLAHE. If beneficial, integrate into the inference pipeline.
plan.success_criteria: CLAHE improves detection_mAP on at least some images. Overall impact quantified.

plan.title: Model quantization: FP16 and INT8 comparison
plan.hypothesis: FP16 export has negligible accuracy loss; INT8 may lose 0.5-2 mAP but significantly reduces model size.
plan.description: Export best YOLO model to ONNX FP16 and INT8. Compare detection_mAP, model size, and inference speed for each. Also test DINOv2 at FP16 vs INT8 for embedding quality.
plan.success_criteria: Quantization impact quantified for each model. Optimal precision level identified for budget constraints.

plan.title: Multi-scale ensemble: same model at different resolutions
plan.hypothesis: Running the same YOLO model at 640 and 1280 and merging with WBF captures both large and small products better.
plan.description: Run YOLOv8x at 640, 1280, and optionally 1920 on val images. Merge with WBF. Compare to single-resolution inference.
plan.success_criteria: Multi-scale ensemble improves detection_mAP over single resolution.

plan.title: Combine tiled inference with TTA
plan.hypothesis: Tiled inference + TTA together provide the maximum detection recall, though at significant inference time cost.
plan.description: Combine SAHI tiling with TTA. Measure detection_mAP and total inference time. Determine if the combination fits within 300s budget.
plan.success_criteria: Combined approach improves detection_mAP. Feasibility within time budget assessed.

plan.title: Corrected annotation weighting
plan.hypothesis: Annotations marked as corrected=True are higher quality. Weighting them more during training improves model quality.
plan.description: Identify corrected annotations in the training data. Implement a training scheme that duplicates or upweights corrected annotations. Retrain and compare val_score.
plan.success_criteria: Corrected annotation weighting improves val_score.

plan.title: Class-balanced sampling / oversampling rare categories
plan.hypothesis: Oversampling images containing rare categories during training improves detection and classification of those categories.
plan.description: Implement class-balanced sampling: oversample images containing categories with <5 annotations. Retrain detector and compare val_score, especially on rare categories.
plan.success_criteria: Rare category performance improves without degrading common category performance.

plan.title: Progressive resizing training
plan.hypothesis: Training at 640 for initial epochs then switching to 1280 converges faster and may generalize better.
plan.description: Train YOLOv8x: first 100 epochs at 640, then resume at 1280 for 200 more epochs. Compare to training at 1280 for all 300 epochs in terms of val_score and total training time.
plan.success_criteria: Progressive resizing achieves comparable or better val_score in less total training time.

plan.title: Embedding-weighted box fusion
plan.hypothesis: When merging overlapping boxes from ensemble models, using DINOv2 embedding agreement as a signal improves both detection and classification quality.
plan.description: Modify WBF to incorporate embedding similarity: when two models predict overlapping boxes, compute DINOv2 embedding similarity between the crops. Weight the merge by both detection confidence and embedding agreement. Compare to standard WBF.
plan.success_criteria: Embedding-weighted fusion improves val_score over standard WBF.

plan.title: Store section-aware classification
plan.hypothesis: Knowing which store section an image belongs to (Egg, Frokost, Knekkebrod, Varmedrikker) narrows the classification search space and improves accuracy.
plan.description: Train a simple image-level classifier to predict store section. Use section prediction to restrict DINOv2 gallery search to only products from that section. Measure classification_mAP improvement.
plan.success_criteria: Section-aware classification improves classification_mAP.

plan.title: Build complete inference pipeline
plan.description: Assemble the best-performing components into a complete inference pipeline: detection (best model/ensemble/tiling), classification (DINOv2 with optimal settings), post-processing (NMS/WBF, thresholds). Profile end-to-end inference time on val split. Ensure it fits within 300s for full test set.
plan.success_criteria: Complete pipeline runs end-to-end. val_score matches or exceeds component-level experiments. Inference time within budget.

plan.title: ONNX export and validation
plan.hypothesis: ONNX export with correct opset (≤20) produces identical results to PyTorch inference.
plan.description: Export best YOLO model and DINOv2 to ONNX FP16. Run inference with onnxruntime-gpu and compare predictions to PyTorch. Verify model sizes fit within 420MB total. Measure ONNX inference speed.
plan.success_criteria: ONNX predictions match PyTorch within tolerance. Total weight size ≤420MB. Inference speed adequate.

plan.title: Soft-NMS vs standard NMS for dense shelves
plan.hypothesis: Soft-NMS preserves more true positives in dense shelf regions where products touch/overlap.
plan.description: Implement Soft-NMS (Gaussian or linear decay) and compare to standard NMS on val split. Sweep sigma parameter. Measure detection_mAP difference.
plan.success_criteria: Soft-NMS improves detection_mAP on dense shelf images.

plan.title: Spatial consistency post-processing
plan.hypothesis: Products on shelves follow spatial patterns (rows, columns). Enforcing spatial consistency in post-processing removes spurious detections and fills gaps.
plan.description: After detection, analyze spatial layout: detect shelf rows, check for gaps that might be missed products, remove detections that don't align with shelf structure. Measure impact on detection_mAP.
plan.success_criteria: Spatial consistency improves detection precision without hurting recall.

plan.title: Neighbor-aware classification
plan.hypothesis: Products are often placed next to identical products on shelves. Using neighboring detection embeddings as context improves classification.
plan.description: For each detection, also consider embeddings of horizontally adjacent detections. If neighbors have high similarity to each other and to a gallery entry, boost that classification. Implement and evaluate on val split.
plan.success_criteria: Neighbor-aware classification improves classification_mAP.

plan.title: YOLOv8x with different augmentation strategies
plan.hypothesis: Tuning augmentation (mosaic probability, mixup, HSV shifts, scale) for shelf images specifically can improve model quality.
plan.description: Train YOLOv8x with different augmentation configs: (1) reduced mosaic (mosaic=0.5), (2) no mixup, (3) stronger HSV augmentation, (4) larger scale range. Compare val_scores.
plan.success_criteria: Optimal augmentation config identified with measurable improvement.

plan.title: Ensemble of nc=1 and nc=357 detectors
plan.hypothesis: Using nc=1 boxes (better recall) with nc=357 class predictions (where confident) and DINOv2 fallback creates the best combined pipeline.
plan.description: Run both nc=1 and nc=357 models. Use nc=1 for box proposals (higher recall). For each box, check if nc=357 model has a confident prediction at the same location; if so, use its class. Otherwise, use DINOv2. Compare to using either model alone.
plan.success_criteria: Combined approach achieves higher val_score than either model alone.

plan.title: DINOv2 with register tokens (DINOv2-reg)
plan.hypothesis: DINOv2 with register tokens produces cleaner embeddings with less artifact noise.
plan.description: If DINOv2 with registers is available in the timm/torch hub version, compare its embeddings to standard DINOv2 for classification quality on val split.
plan.success_criteria: Register-token DINOv2 improves classification accuracy.

plan.title: Lightweight classifier head on YOLO features
plan.hypothesis: Training a separate classification head on YOLO's intermediate features (before the detection head) could provide better classification than the default YOLO class output.
plan.description: Extract feature maps from YOLO's backbone for each detection ROI. Train a small classifier head (FC layers) on these features using training annotations. Compare classification quality to YOLO's built-in classification and DINOv2.
plan.success_criteria: Custom classifier head improves classification over default YOLO class predictions.

plan.title: Optimal detection confidence threshold for mAP
plan.hypothesis: Very low confidence thresholds (0.001-0.01) maximize mAP since COCO evaluation handles precision-recall internally.
plan.description: Sweep detection confidence threshold from 0.001 to 0.5 and measure val_score at each level. The COCO mAP metric computes its own precision-recall curve, so submitting more predictions (lower threshold) might help if they include true positives.
plan.success_criteria: Optimal confidence threshold identified for maximum val_score.

plan.title: Optimize inference speed for 300s budget
plan.description: Profile the complete pipeline on val split. Identify bottlenecks (detection, crop extraction, DINOv2 embedding, kNN lookup). Optimize: batch DINOv2 inference, pre-compute gallery, use ONNX runtime, reduce unnecessary computation. Estimate total time for ~50-100 test images.
plan.success_criteria: Pipeline runs within 300s for estimated test set size. Bottlenecks identified and mitigated.

plan.title: Batch DINOv2 inference optimization
plan.hypothesis: Batching DINOv2 crop embeddings (instead of one-by-one) significantly reduces classification inference time.
plan.description: Implement batched DINOv2 inference: collect all crops from an image, batch them (batch_size=32 or 64), compute embeddings in one forward pass. Measure speedup vs sequential processing.
plan.success_criteria: Batched inference is at least 2x faster than sequential. No accuracy change.

plan.title: FAISS for fast kNN lookup
plan.hypothesis: FAISS index for gallery lookup is faster than brute-force numpy distance computation, especially with 357 categories and many gallery entries.
plan.description: Build a FAISS index (IndexFlatIP for cosine similarity) from the gallery embeddings. Compare lookup speed and accuracy to numpy-based kNN. Note: check if FAISS is available in sandbox or if we need a pure-numpy fallback.
plan.success_criteria: FAISS lookup is faster. Classification accuracy is identical.

plan.title: Augmented gallery with synthetic variations
plan.hypothesis: Augmenting gallery entries with brightness/contrast/rotation variations makes the gallery more robust to real-world appearance variations.
plan.description: For each reference product image, create 5 augmented versions (brightness ±20%, slight rotation, horizontal flip, color jitter). Add their embeddings to the gallery. Measure classification accuracy change on val split.
plan.success_criteria: Augmented gallery improves classification accuracy.

plan.title: Weighted ensemble of classification methods
plan.hypothesis: A weighted combination of YOLO class probabilities and DINOv2 similarity scores produces better classification than either alone.
plan.description: For each detection, compute: (1) YOLO class probability vector (357-dim), (2) DINOv2 kNN similarity-based probability vector. Combine with learned weights: final_prob = α * yolo_prob + (1-α) * dino_prob. Sweep α on val split.
plan.success_criteria: Optimal α found. Weighted combination outperforms either method alone.

plan.title: Write submission run.py
plan.description: Write the final run.py that: reads images from --input, runs the complete pipeline (detection, classification, post-processing), outputs predictions.json to --output. Ensure it uses only allowed imports (pathlib not os, json not yaml, no blocked modules). Test locally.
plan.success_criteria: run.py runs correctly on val images, produces valid COCO-format predictions, uses only allowed imports.

plan.title: Package submission zip
plan.description: Create submission.zip with: run.py, model weights (≤3 files, ≤420MB total), gallery data, any helper .py files. Verify: total uncompressed size ≤420MB, no .bin files, all weights are .pt/.onnx/.safetensors.
plan.success_criteria: Valid submission zip created. Size within limits. All files present.

plan.title: End-to-end validation of submission
plan.hypothesis: The packaged submission produces the same val_score as the development pipeline.
plan.description: Unzip submission to a clean directory. Run run.py on val images. Evaluate predictions.json with the evaluation function. Verify val_score matches development results. Time the full run.
plan.success_criteria: Submission val_score matches development. Inference completes within 300s equivalent.

plan.title: Ablation study: contribution of each component
plan.description: Systematically disable each pipeline component and measure val_score impact: (1) no tiling, (2) no TTA, (3) no DINOv2 (detection only), (4) no ensemble, (5) default thresholds. Document the contribution of each component.
plan.success_criteria: Clear understanding of each component's contribution to final val_score.

plan.title: Document best configuration for human operator
plan.description: Write a clear summary of: best model configuration, training hyperparameters, inference pipeline settings, val_score achieved, and instructions for the human to retrain on full 248 images. Include all relevant file paths and commands.
plan.success_criteria: Complete documentation that enables the human to reproduce and retrain the best configuration.
